rationale: Matthew 13:43 reads “Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father” (BSB); Daniel 12:3 reads “Then the wise will shine like the brightness of the heavens” (BSB). Both follow a separation at the end: Daniel 12:2 has some rising “to everlasting life” and others “to shame and everlasting contempt,” and Matthew 13:41-42 has the weeds removed before the righteous shine. In Greek, Matthew’s verb eklampsousin also stands in the Greek Daniel 12:3 served by Blue Letter Bible, though not in the Greek text Bible Hub serves as Swete’s (phanousin), and Bengel notes that the Septuagint uses the same verb. Calvin writes that “our Lord unquestionably refers here to a passage in Daniel” (12:3), and the Pulpit Commentary calls it “An undoubted reference to the substance of Daniel 12:3.” Graded allusion, not quotation, because there is no formula and the wording differs (“sun” against “brightness of the heavens”); strong, not plausible, because the shared verb, the shared end-time setting and named commentators all point to the same verse. In the BSB, “shine like the sun” also occurs at Judges 5:31, which no commentator read here connects to 13:43.
